root_cause.text: The driver was incorrectly attempting to transmit garbage data during emulated read-only dual/quad SPI operations by calling `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()` instead of `mchp_coreqspi_read_op()`, which corrupted transfers on a bus without a dedicated master-out line.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `dual_quad` flag to detect when dual or quad mode is used (checking `SPI_NBITS_QUAD` and `SPI_NBITS_DUAL` on both tx and rx), then conditionally routes dual/quad read operations to `mchp_coreqspi_read_op()` instead of `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()`. The commit message explicitly states that "transmitting garbage data just bricks the transfer since QSPI doesn't have a dedicated master-out line like MOSI in regular SPI," indicating the original code was incorrectly treating dual/quad reads as write-read operations when they should be read-only operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix SPI quad/dual mode transfers by routing them to the correct read operation instead of incorrectly using write-read for dual/quad capable transfers.
intent_record.what: Added a `dual_quad` boolean flag that detects quad or dual SPI mode transfers, then modified the conditional logic to branch into three paths: (1) write-only when no rx_buf, (2) write-read operation when rx_buf exists and NOT in dual/quad mode, and (3) read-only operation when rx_buf exists and IS in dual/quad mode.
intent_record.how: Previously, any transfer with an rx_buf would execute the write-read operation regardless of SPI mode. Now, dual/quad mode transfers with rx_buf will invoke `mchp_coreqspi_read_op()` instead of `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()`, allowing the hardware to handle quad/dual reads with the appropriate operation sequence rather than attempting a combined write-read in those modes.

According to the root cause, emulated read-only dual/quad SPI operations should call mchp_coreqspi_read_op() instead of mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op(), which transmits garbage data and corrupts transfers on buses without a dedicated master-out line.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement at line 704 incorrectly calls mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op() for emulated read-only dual/quad SPI operations. The write-read operation transmits garbage data on the master-out line, corrupting transfers on buses without a dedicated master-out line. The fix routes these operations to mchp_coreqspi_read_op() instead, which performs read-only operations without transmitting spurious data.

commit 8f9cf02c8852837923f1cdacfcc92e138513325c
Author: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 20 14:28:26 2025 +0100

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers
    
    The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
    add support for regular transfers so that the SD card slot and ADC on
    the BeagleV Fire can be used.
    
    Signed-off-by: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
    Co-developed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()` function and the `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()` function that calls it. The vulnerability root cause describes that the driver incorrectly calls `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()` instead of `mchp_coreqspi_read_op()` for read-only dual/quad SPI operations. However, in this commit, there is no `mchp_coreqspi_read_op()` function defined anywhere in the diff, and the `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()` function (lines 676-688) simply checks `if (!t->rx_buf)` to call `mchp_coreqspi_write_op()`, otherwise it calls `mchp_coreqspi_write_read_op()`. The vulnerable construct (incorrectly calling write_read_op for read-only operations) is not present in this code - the function correctly distinguishes between write-only and write-read operations. The bug would be introduced in a later commit that adds a `mchp_coreqspi_read_op()` function but fails to use it in the appropriate cases.
